meta.title: Japan in Autumn, Unhurried
meta.budgetNote: land only; ≈ US$7,650 with US$215/night hotels

profile: Plan an 18-day autumn trip to Japan for two, 10–27 November 2026. We land at Narita at 19:45 and leave from Narita Terminal 3 at 13:45. Unhurried and anti-crowd: 8,000–12,000 steps a day, taxis between hills, only 3 hotel moves. We love ancient, Edo and modern history, nature and autumn leaves (one gentle hike under 5 hours), the JDM car scene, second-hand watches, English bookshops and stationery. One private-onsen ryokan. One of you eats everything; the other is pescatarian (no land meat, fish dashi is fine). Land budget US$7,000–8,000 for two, excluding flights and shopping.

days.title: Land at Narita, straight to bed
days.purpose: Arrive, get through the airport with your phones ready, and sleep. About 3,000 steps.
watch: Pick the hotel near your airport train: Skyliner → Ueno, N'EX → Tokyo Station

items.t: Land at Narita; immigration and customs
items.n: Have your Visit Japan Web QR codes screenshotted on both phones; allow 45–60 min.

items.t: Add Suica or Pasmo in Apple Wallet; take ¥20,000 from the 7-Bank ATM in arrivals
items.n: No queue at the ticket machines with a phone card.

items.t: Keisei Skyliner, 41 min non-stop to Keisei Ueno
items.n: Or the Narita Express (55 min) to Tokyo Station if you pick The Gate Hotel.

items.t: Check in at NOHGA HOTEL UENO TOKYO
items.n: Quiet side street 5 min from Keisei Ueno. Alternatives: The Gate Hotel Tokyo (Yurakucho) or MIMARU SUITES Nihombashi.

items.t: 7-Eleven snack (kombu or salmon onigiri, egg sando, hot tea), then sleep

days.title: Imperial history, book town and Senso-ji at night
days.purpose: Sleep in, then Edo Castle's walls, Jimbocho's old bookshops and Senso-ji once the crowds have gone. About 8,500 steps.
watch: Book Manten Sushi on TableCheck before you fly

items.t: Slow coffee at Bongen Coffee
items.n: Or Leaves Coffee Apartment.

items.t: Imperial Palace East Gardens: Edo Castle keep foundations, moats and stone walls
items.n: Open Wednesdays, free, spacious and quiet.

items.t: Lunch: 25-piece seasonal omakase at Manten Sushi Marunouchi
items.n: Tabelog 3.60; about ¥4,400 a person. Book ahead on TableCheck. All fish and vegetables.

items.t: Jimbocho Book Town: Kitazawa Bookstore (2F) and Isseido Booksellers
items.n: Kitazawa is open 12:00–17:00: rare English books and classics in a library-like room.

items.t: Rest your feet at Sabouru, a 1955 kissaten
Dinner: charcoal-grilled unagi at Sumiyaki Unafuji Yurakucho
items.n: Tabelog 3.68. Or Asakusa Unana, closer to Senso-ji.

items.t: Senso-ji after dark: the lanterns and five-storey pagoda lit, the crowds gone
items.n: Nakamise Street is packed 10:00–17:00; at 20:00 it's empty.

days.title: The reopened Edo-Tokyo Museum and old Yanaka
days.purpose: How samurai-era Edo became Tokyo, then the neighbourhood that survived both the 1923 earthquake and the war. About 9,500 steps.

items.t: Edo-Tokyo Museum, Ryogoku: life-size Nihonbashi bridge and Edo towns
items.n: Reopened 31 March 2026 after four years; open 9:30–17:30, ¥800. Closed Mondays.

items.t: Lunch: Ramen Takahashi Ginza, flying-fish (ago-dashi) broth
items.n: Show the dietary card and ask for the pure seafood broth. Or T's Tantan at Tokyo Station (fully plant-based tantanmen).

items.t: Yanaka Ginza shopping street
items.n: One of the few Tokyo neighbourhoods that survived 1923 and WWII.

items.t: Coffee at Kayaba Coffee, a 1916 wooden townhouse
Nezu Shrine's quiet vermilion torii tunnel
items.n: Tokyo's uncrowded answer to Fushimi Inari.

items.t: Dinner: charcoal-grilled nodoguro and sashimi at Nodoguro no Nakamata
items.n: Tabelog 3.57.

days.title: Samurai treasures in Ueno and a Friday car meet
days.purpose: Forward the big bags to Kyoto, see the samurai swords and armour, then Kuramae's makers — and, if you book it, Daikoku PA on its busiest night. About 8,000 steps.
planB: Rain: move Daikoku PA to Tuesday 24 Nov and have an early night.
days.spend: The guided JDM Car Club ride-along (≈ US$245 for two) — the only safe way in and out of Daikoku PA.

items.t: Forward the main suitcases to the Kyoto hotel (Yamato Takkyubin)
items.n: Front desk fills in the slip, about ¥2,500 a bag. They arrive by 16 Nov; take only a 2-night bag to Fuji.

items.t: Tokyo National Museum, Honkan: samurai swords, armour, tea rooms
items.n: Through Ueno Park's golden ginkgos. Ground floor only, to dodge museum fatigue. Open Fridays until 20:00.

items.t: Kakimori, Kuramae: design a custom-bound notebook
items.n: Open 11:00–18:00; closed Mondays. Mix-your-own fountain pen ink too.

items.t: Pour-over at Leaves Coffee Roasters
items.n: Or Sol's Coffee.

items.t: Optional: JDM Car Club ride-along — pickup, then A-PIT Autobacs Shinonome
items.n: Book the guided ride-along: no trains reach Daikoku PA and taxis will strand you there.

items.t: Optional: Daikoku PA, Friday peak night — Skylines, RX-7s, kaido racers
items.n: About 90 min at the PA, then drop-off at the hotel. Backup: Tue 24 Nov.

days.title: Scenic train to Mt Fuji and a private onsen
days.purpose: Ride out to the lake with a light bag and spend the afternoon in your own open-air hot spring facing Fuji. About 5,500 steps.
days.spend: The room with a private open-air hot-spring bath facing Fuji — it's the point of these two nights.
watch: Request the pescatarian kaiseki when you book, at least 5–7 days ahead

items.t: JR Fuji Excursion limited express from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko
items.n: About 1 h 55 min; or the highway bus from Tokyo Station Yaesu South Exit.

items.t: Lunch: mushroom and vegetable miso houtou at Houtou Fudou
items.n: The cloud-shaped building. Confirm niku-nashi (no pork); or Kosaku (Tabelog 3.49).

items.t: Check in at Konansou: room with a private open-air onsen and Fuji view
items.n: Alternatives: Bessho Sasa, Fufu Kawaguchiko, Ubuya. Ask for pescatarian kaiseki 5–7 days ahead.

items.t: Soak in the room's rotenburo and watch the sun set behind Fuji
Autumn seafood kaiseki dinner at the ryokan
items.n: Pre-arranged as seafood-only for the pescatarian.

days.title: Itchiku kimono, lakeside walk and the lit Momiji Corridor
days.purpose: Red Fuji at dawn from the bath, Kubota Itchiku's kimonos, a flat lakeside walk and the maple corridor lit up at dusk. About 7,500 steps.

items.t: Akafuji: Mt Fuji and its reflection from your balcony bath
items.n: Best visibility 6:00–8:30 in November, before midday clouds.

items.t: Kubota Itchiku Art Museum: silk kimonos in a maple garden
items.n: Open 10:00–17:00. Tearoom looks at Fuji.

items.t: Flat lakeside walk at Nagasaki Park
items.n: Quieter than Oishi Park, with cleaner Fuji framing.

items.t: Back to the ryokan for an afternoon soak
Momiji Corridor at the Autumn Leaves Festival, lit until 21:00
items.n: 60+ giant maples on an old canal, forecast to peak around 15–17 Nov. Festival runs 7–29 Nov.

items.t: Second kaiseki dinner at the ryokan

days.title: Around Mt Fuji to Kyoto, then Gion at dusk
days.purpose: Bus to Mishima and the shinkansen to Kyoto, where your bags are waiting; an easy first stroll through Gion. About 7,000 steps.

items.t: Fujikyu express bus, Kawaguchiko Station → Mishima Station
items.n: About 1 h 30 min. Pre-book seats on sekitori.jp.

items.t: Hikari shinkansen, Mishima → Kyoto
items.n: About 2 h 05 min.

items.t: Check in at THE BLOSSOM KYOTO; the suitcases are already there
items.n: Alternatives: Nohga Hotel Kiyomizu, The Thousand Kyoto.

items.t: Orientation stroll along the Kamogawa
Shirakawa Minami-dori, Gion's prettiest, quietest willow-lined lane
Yasaka Shrine, lantern-lit after dusk
items.n: Open 24/7.

items.t: Dinner: obanzai, yuba and seasonal sashimi at Tousuiro Gion
items.n: Tabelog 3.45. Or Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera Kyoto (3.48).

days.title: Daitoku-ji's Zen sub-temples and Nijo Castle
days.purpose: Skip the Kinkaku-ji crush for a walled city of Zen temples, a temple lunch on tatami and the Shogun's palace. About 8,500 steps.

items.t: Daitoku-ji: Daisen-in, Zuiho-in and Ryogen-in
items.n: One of Japan's great 16th-century dry gardens; few tourists come this far north.

items.t: Lunch: shojin ryori in red lacquer bowls at Izusen, facing a moss garden
items.n: Open 11:00–16:00; all plant and kelp dashi.

items.t: Nijo Castle: the Ninomaru Palace's nightingale floors and gardens
items.n: Closes 17:00, last entry 16:00.

items.t: Drinks at Bee's Knees, then seafood robatayaki at Tai no Tai Karasuma
items.n: Or a quiet evening at the hotel.

days.title: Arashiyama from the top: the downhill route
days.purpose: Taxi to the head of the valley and walk only downhill through moss-covered statues, a thatched-roof street and red maples to a Zen lunch. About 9,500 steps, almost all downhill or flat.
days.spend: The taxi up the valley (about ¥2,000) — it turns a crowded uphill slog into a quiet downhill walk.

items.t: Taxi to the top of the valley
Otagi Nenbutsu-ji: 1,200 moss-covered stone rakan
items.n: In total forest quiet at opening time.

items.t: Walk down the Meiji-era thatched-roof street of Saga-Toriimoto
Adashino Nenbutsu-ji and its own uncrowded bamboo grove
Jojakko-ji's blazing maples
Tenryu-ji's UNESCO landscape garden
Lunch: Zen vegetarian cuisine at Shigetsu, inside Tenryu-ji
items.n: Michelin Bib Gourmand, Tabelog 3.80; open 11:00–14:00. Reserve ahead.

items.t: Togetsukyo Bridge, then the Randen tram back for a restful late afternoon

days.title: Nature day: Eizan maple tunnel and Kifune
days.purpose: Ride through the maple tunnel into the cedar forest, walk to Kifune Shrine (or over the ridge from Kurama) and ride back through the illuminated tunnel. About 9,000–12,000 steps.
planB: Tired: do only the gentle Kifune walk and skip Kurama.
watch: Check whether the Kurama cable car is running before choosing the hike

items.t: Eizan Electric Railway from Demachiyanagi, through the Momiji Tunnel
items.n: About 30 min north; ¥470. Check at the station whether the Kurama cable car is running.

items.t: Gentle option: shuttle up the gorge to Kifune Shrine, walk the river path to the Okumiya
items.n: Red-lantern stone staircase and floating water fortunes; matcha and sweets by the stream. 2–3 h, easy on the knees.

items.t: Or the full hike: Kurama-dera, then the 3.9 km cedar-root trail over the ridge to Kifune
items.n: 2.5–3 h for the trail; 3.5–4 h with Kurama-dera. Pick on the morning by your energy.

items.t: Ride back at dusk through the lit maple tunnel
items.n: The train dims its lights and slows down. Illumination 10–28 Nov.

days.title: Quiet eastern gardens and Eikan-do's opening night
days.purpose: Shoren-in and Nanzen-ji in the morning, a 560-year-old soba house for lunch, a rest, then Kyoto's most famous maple illumination on its first night. About 8,500 steps.

items.t: Shoren-in: 800-year-old camphor trees, tatami halls, pond garden
Nanzen-ji: the Sanmon gate, the Meiji brick aqueduct and Tenju-an's maple garden
Lunch: Hourai Soba at Honke Owariya, founded 1465
items.n: Kombu and bonito dashi. Or yudofu at Nanzen-ji Junsei.

items.t: Rest at the hotel so your feet are fresh for the evening
Eikan-do Autumn Night Illumination, opening night
items.n: 17:30–20:30, ¥1,000; 20 Nov – 6 Dec. 3,000 maples reflected in the Hojo Pond under the lit pagoda.

days.title: Early Fushimi Inari and the Heian matcha town of Uji
days.purpose: Fushimi Inari before the Saturday crowds, then Byodo-in, Japan's oldest shrine building and stone-ground matcha in calm Uji. About 9,500 steps.

items.t: Fushimi Inari: the flat lower Senbon Torii loop and the quiet bamboo side path
items.n: Open 24/7; only the lower loop, about 45 min.

items.t: JR Nara Line south to Uji
items.n: About 20 min.

items.t: Byodo-in: the Phoenix Hall (1053) on its reflection pond
items.n: The building on the ¥10 coin.

items.t: Cross the river to Ujigami Shrine, c. 1060
items.n: The oldest original Shinto shrine building in Japan.

items.t: Matcha and green-tea soba at Nakamura Tokichi Honten (since 1854)
Optional: Kodai-ji night illumination
items.n: 17:00–21:30, ¥800. Or Kiyomizu-dera's special night viewing (from 21 Nov, until 21:30, ¥500).

days.title: Nara's ancient forest, or a slow Kyoto day
days.purpose: Send the bags to Tokyo, then either half a day in Nara — downhill from Nigatsu-do through the lantern forest to the Great Buddha — or a slow day of books and gardens in Kyoto. About 8,000–10,000 steps.
planB: Slow Kyoto day instead: sleep in, Keibunsha Ichijoji bookshop, Kyoto Botanical Gardens or Honen-in, and a farewell seafood dinner.

items.t: Forward the suitcases to the Ginza hotel (Yamato Takkyubin)
items.n: So you ride the shinkansen hands-free tomorrow.

items.t: Kintetsu limited express to Nara (all seats reserved)
items.n: About 35 min.

items.t: Taxi up to Nigatsu-do's wooden balcony over Nara
items.n: Free and quiet.

items.t: Walk gently downhill through the lantern-lined forest to Kasuga Taisha
Todai-ji: the world's largest bronze Buddha (752)
Lunch in Naramachi, the preserved Edo merchant district

days.title: Back to Tokyo: Daikanyama books and Nakameguro
days.purpose: Shinkansen back with Fuji out of the window, then Tokyo's most relaxed low-rise neighbourhoods and a splurge sushi counter. About 8,500 steps.
days.spend: Udatsu Sushi — one of the three splurge meals.

items.t: Nozomi shinkansen, Kyoto → Tokyo
items.n: Reserve seats D and E for the Mt Fuji view. About 2 h 13 min.

items.t: Drop the small bag at Karaksa Hotel Premier Tokyo Ginza
items.n: Alternatives: The Gate Hotel Tokyo, MUJI Hotel Ginza.

items.t: Daikanyama T-Site: international book pavilions, then coffee in the Anjin lounge
Traveler's Factory Nakameguro, the back-alley stationery flagship
Independent boutiques along the Meguro River
Splurge: omakase at Udatsu Sushi
items.n: Michelin-starred, Tabelog 3.68. Book via Pocket Concierge or the official site. Or Sushi Tokyo Ten, Roppongi.

days.title: Nakano Broadway watch hunt and Shinjuku books
days.purpose: A garden at peak colour, a whole floor of English books, then the watch dealers of Nakano Broadway once they're open. About 9,000 steps.
watch: Physical passport for tax-free; tell your bank about a large JPY purchase or bring two cards

items.t: Morning walk in Shinjuku Gyoen's maple valleys
items.n: Late-November peak colour.

items.t: Books Kinokuniya Tokyo: a floor of English books
items.n: Takashimaya Times Square South Bldg, 6F; 10:30–19:30. Not the Shinjuku Main Store.

items.t: Lunch: clam and sea-bream broth at SOBAHOUSE Konjiki Hototogisu
items.n: Tabelog 3.75+. Confirm the pure shellfish/fish soup at the counter.

items.t: Watch hunt: Jackroad, Kame-Kichi and Watchnian (3F); Fire Kids and Cheese (1F)
items.n: JR Chuo Line, one stop from Shinjuku. Shops open 11:00–12:00 — never before 11:30. Bring your physical passport for 10% tax-free.

items.t: Optional backup night for the car scene: A-PIT Autobacs Shinonome or a guided Daikoku run
items.n: Only if Friday 13 Nov was rained out. A-PIT is open until 21:00, 1 min from Shinonome Station.

days.title: Nezu Museum garden, Aoyama and Rikugien's light-up
days.purpose: A hidden maple ravine behind Kengo Kuma's museum, an afternoon of Aoyama and Harajuku backstreets, and Rikugien lit on its first night. About 9,500 steps.

items.t: Nezu Museum and its strolling garden at peak maple
items.n: Open 10:00–17:00. Pre-book timed entry online.

items.t: Aoyama and Omotesando: heritage denim, Issey Miyake / Homme Plissé, Kapital, Beams Plus, Snow Peak
Coffee at Koffee Mameya
Harajuku backstreets along Cat Street
items.n: Or: the Louvre Renaissance masterpieces show at the National Art Center (9 Sep – 13 Dec; Wed 10:00–18:00).

items.t: Rikugien Autumn Leaves Light-Up, opening night
items.n: 18:00–20:30, 25 Nov – 6 Dec. A 1702 feudal lord's garden; weeping maples and teahouses over the pond.

days.title: Last shopping day: Ginza watches, Itoya and Tsutaya
days.purpose: The forecast peak for Tokyo's golden ginkgos. Stationery, a farewell tempura lunch and a four-block loop of watches, books and tech. About 8,500 steps.
days.spend: Tempura Kondo — the last of the three splurge meals.

items.t: Ginza Itoya (G.Itoya and K.Itoya): 12 floors of pens, paper and travel gear
items.n: Opens 10:00.

items.t: Farewell splurge: tempura lunch at Tempura Kondo
items.n: Two Michelin stars; sesame-oil seafood and sweet-potato tempura. Or Tempura Yokota.

items.t: Ginza watch loop: Shellman, Watchnian Ginza, Rasin and Seiko House (Wako)
items.n: Shellman 11:00–19:30; Watchnian 11:00–20:00.

items.t: Seiko House Ginza (Wako)
Ginza Tsutaya Books (GINZA SIX, 6F), then omiyage in the basement food hall
items.n: Art, architecture, photography and craft monographs.

items.t: Tech and cameras at Bic Camera Yurakucho

days.title: Easy morning, then fly home from Narita T3

plan:
# Japan in Autumn, Unhurried — Tue 10 Nov to Fri 27 Nov 2026

## Summary

- **18 days, 17 nights, only 3 hotel moves:** {{tokyo}} (4 nights, Ueno) → {{kawaguchiko}} (2 nights, private-onsen ryokan) → {{kyoto}} (7 nights) → {{tokyo}} (4 nights, Ginza).
- **Arrive** Narita 19:45, Tue 10 Nov. **Leave** Narita Terminal 3 at 13:45, Fri 27 Nov.
- **Pace:** unhurried and anti-crowd, 8,000–12,000 steps a day, taxis between hills so you walk downhill.
- **Land budget for two:** ≈ US$8,100, or ≈ US$7,650 with ~US$215/night hotels (target US$7,000–8,000, excluding flights and shopping).
- **Diet:** One of you eats everything; the other is pescatarian (fish, seafood, dashi, eggs, dairy; no land meat).

## Why these dates work
- Kawaguchiko's lakeside maples peak around 17 Nov; the Momiji Corridor is lit until 21:00 from 7 to 29 Nov.
- Kyoto's northern temples peak mid-November, and the night illuminations overlap your last Kyoto nights: Kodai-ji, To-ji, Eikan-do (from 20 Nov) and Kiyomizu-dera (from 21 Nov).
- Tokyo's ginkgos peak around 26 Nov and its maples around 28 Nov; Rikugien's light-up starts 25 Nov.

## What was cut, and why
| Cut | Why | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| Kanazawa, Takayama, Shirakawa-go | 2 extra hotel moves, 7+ h of transfers | Edo streetscapes in Yanaka, Saga-Toriimoto and Naramachi |
| Hiroshima and Miyajima | 4.5 h round trip or another hotel | Short trips to {{byodoin}} in Uji and {{todaiji}} in Nara from one Kyoto hotel |
| Hakone as well as Kawaguchiko | Moving bags across mountain buses | Kawaguchiko only: bigger, clearer Fuji views and the maple festival |
| Six-temple Kyoto days | 24,000 steps and burnout | One anchor each morning and a calm afternoon, with GO Taxi between hills |

## Avoiding the crowds
| Icon | Timing | Quieter twin |
|---|---|---|
| Arashiyama Bamboo Grove | 7:30 | Taxi up to {{otagi}}, walk downhill via {{adashino}}'s own bamboo grove |
| {{fushimi-inari}} | 7:15, lower loop only | The Take-no-Michi bamboo path, or {{nezu-shrine}} in Tokyo |
| Kinkaku-ji | 8:50 for the 9:00 opening | Ginkaku-ji, Honen-in, {{nanzenji}}'s Tenju-an |
| {{kiyomizu}} | 7:00, or the night viewing from 21 Nov | {{shorenin}} and Chion-in |
| {{sensoji}} | 20:30, lit and empty | Fukagawa Fudo-do's goma fire ritual, Yanaka's temples |

## Where you'll stay
- {{hotel-ueno}} — Ueno, Days 1–4 (≈ US$235/night). Alternatives: The Gate Hotel Tokyo, MIMARU SUITES Nihombashi.
- {{konansou}} — Kawaguchiko, Days 5–6 (≈ US$625/night with two kaiseki dinners and breakfasts; room with a private open-air onsen facing Fuji). Alternatives: Bessho Sasa at Kaneyamaen, Fufu Kawaguchiko, Ubuya.
- {{hotel-kyoto}} — Kyoto, Days 7–13 (≈ US$245/night). Alternatives: Nohga Hotel Kiyomizu, The Thousand Kyoto.
- {{hotel-ginza}} — Ginza, Days 14–17 (≈ US$265/night). Alternatives: The Gate Hotel Tokyo, MUJI Hotel Ginza.

## Budget for two (land only)
| | |
|---|---|
| Hotels, 17 nights | US$4,965 |
| Food and coffee (≈ US$105/day + 3 splurges: Udatsu, Tempura Kondo, Shigetsu) | US$1,900 |
| Trains, buses, taxis, 3 luggage transfers | US$850 |
| Entries, illuminations, JDM car tour | US$385 |
| **Total** | **≈ US$8,100** (≈ US$7,650 on US$215/night hotels) |

## Day by day
1. **Tue 10 Nov, Land at Narita, straight to bed**
2. **Wed 11 Nov, Imperial history, book town and Senso-ji at night**
3. **Thu 12 Nov, The reopened Edo-Tokyo Museum and old Yanaka**
4. **Fri 13 Nov, Samurai treasures in Ueno and a Friday car meet** (bags forwarded to Kyoto)
5. **Sat 14 Nov, Scenic train to Mt Fuji and a private onsen**
6. **Sun 15 Nov, Itchiku kimono, lakeside walk and the lit Momiji Corridor**
7. **Mon 16 Nov, Around Mt Fuji to Kyoto, then Gion at dusk**
8. **Tue 17 Nov, Daitoku-ji's Zen sub-temples and Nijo Castle**
9. **Wed 18 Nov, Arashiyama from the top: the downhill route**
10. **Thu 19 Nov, Nature day: Eizan maple tunnel and Kifune**
11. **Fri 20 Nov, Quiet eastern gardens and Eikan-do's opening night**
12. **Sat 21 Nov, Early Fushimi Inari and Uji**
13. **Sun 22 Nov, Nara's ancient forest, or a slow Kyoto day** (bags forwarded to Ginza)
14. **Mon 23 Nov, Back to Tokyo: Daikanyama books and Nakameguro**
15. **Tue 24 Nov, Nakano Broadway watch hunt and Shinjuku books**
16. **Wed 25 Nov, Nezu Museum garden, Aoyama and Rikugien's light-up**
17. **Thu 26 Nov, Last shopping day: Ginza watches, Itoya and Tsutaya**
18. **Fri 27 Nov, Easy morning, then fly home from Narita T3**

## Good to know
- **Pescatarian traps:** ramen stock (tonkotsu, tori paitan), gyoza fried in lard and curry roux hide meat. Safe: sushi, sashimi, tempura, unagi, shojin ryori, yudofu, zaru or kake soba (avoid kamo and kashiwa soba). Show this card:
  > 私は魚介類・魚の出汁・卵・乳製品は食べられますが、肉類（牛肉・豚肉・鶏肉・鴨・ベーコン・ラード・肉のエキスや鶏ガラスープ／豚骨スープ）は一切食べられません。魚介と昆布・椎茸の出汁のみの料理を教えていただけますか？ありがとうございます！
- **Luggage:** two medium spinners (60–68 cm), not one bag over 160 cm (shinkansen oversize seats need booking), plus a flat duffel for shopping. Yamato Takkyubin (≈ ¥2,500 a bag): Tokyo → Kyoto on 13 Nov, Kyoto → Ginza on 22 Nov.
- **Steps:** the 20,000-step days come from subway transfer tunnels and Kyoto bus queues. Install GO Taxi and Uber; a 15-min Kyoto taxi is ¥1,200–2,200 for two.
- **Shopping:** carry the physical passport for 10% tax-free; warn your bank or carry two cards; Nakano Broadway opens 11:00–12:00.
- **Cash and cards:** Suica or Pasmo in Apple Wallet; keep ¥15,000–20,000 cash for temples, omikuji and ramen ticket machines.
- **Temples:** slip-on shoes and warm socks — you'll take your shoes off often and the floors are cold in November.

chat.md: Plan an 18-day autumn trip to Japan for two, 10–27 November 2026. We land at Narita at 19:45 and leave from Narita Terminal 3 at 13:45. Unhurried and anti-crowd: 8,000–12,000 steps a day, taxis between hills, only 3 hotel moves. We love ancient, Edo and modern history, nature and autumn leaves (one gentle hike under 5 hours), the JDM car scene, second-hand watches, English bookshops and stationery. One private-onsen ryokan. One of you eats everything; the other is pescatarian (no land meat, fish dashi is fine). Land budget US$7,000–8,000 for two, excluding flights and shopping.

Here's the unhurried version: {{tokyo}} → {{kawaguchiko}} under Mt Fuji → a full week in {{kyoto}} with day trips to Uji and Nara → {{tokyo}} for watches, books and the last of the foliage. Only three hotel moves, two luggage forwards, and every day kept to about 8,000–12,000 steps. It comes to about **US$8,100** for the two of you on the land side, or about US$7,650 with slightly cheaper hotels.

The whole plan is in the itinerary, calendar and map. Ask me to move, add or drop anything — I'll show the changes for you to approve first.
